blocks.text: Agricultural productivity depends on **irrigation and modern inputs** — **HYV seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, credit and mechanisation** — that powered the **Green Revolution**. India has diverse irrigation sources but faces **water stress and over-reliance on groundwater**.

rows: **Wells & tube-wells (largest, ~groundwater), canals, tanks**; net irrigated area rising.
**HYV seeds, chemical fertilizers, pesticides, assured irrigation, mechanisation**.
**Groundwater depletion, waterlogging/salinity, soil degradation, input subsidy burden**.
**PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY), Soil Health Card, Neem-coated urea**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: irrigation, water & inputs

items: **Irrigation sources**: **canals, tanks, wells & tube-wells (largest & growing — groundwater is ~60% of irrigation)**; India is the world's **largest groundwater extractor** → over-exploitation blocks.
**Micro-irrigation**: drip & sprinkler ('**Per Drop More Crop**', PMKSY); watershed development.
**Inputs**: HYV seeds, chemical fertilizers (urea subsidy, Nutrient-Based Subsidy, neem-coated urea), pesticides, mechanisation, credit; **soil health cards**.
**PMKSY (Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana)** — 'Har Khet Ko Pani'; **Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme**; interlinking of rivers.
**AP**: heavy canal irrigation from **Krishna & Godavari** (Nagarjunasagar, Srisailam, **Polavaram** multipurpose project); tank irrigation; groundwater in Rayalaseema.
Wells/tube-wells = largest irrigation source (groundwater); Green Revolution inputs = HYV+fertilizer+irrigation.
Micro-irrigation (drip/sprinkler) via PMKSY 'Per Drop More Crop'.

**Soil Health Card** scheme promotes balanced fertilizer use.
Concerns — **groundwater depletion, waterlogging, salinity, fertilizer subsidy burden**.
Largest irrigation source = **wells/tube-wells (groundwater)**; India = world's biggest groundwater user.
**PMKSY** = 'Har Khet Ko Pani' + 'Per Drop More Crop' (micro-irrigation).

mainsAngles: Discuss the role of irrigation and inputs in Indian agriculture.

glossary.definition: The late-1960s leap in food-grain output via HYV seeds, fertilizers and irrigation.
High-Yielding Variety seeds central to the Green Revolution.
The Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana, India's umbrella irrigation programme.

blocks.text: India's **agricultural strategy** evolved from the **Green Revolution's productivity focus to diversification, allied activities and doubling farmers' income**. Yet an **agrarian crisis** — low incomes, indebtedness, price volatility and farmer distress — persists, driving policy reform.

rows: **Green Revolution → diversification (horticulture, dairy, fisheries) → income focus (doubling farmers' income by 2022 target)**.
**Green (foodgrains), White/Operation Flood (milk — Kurien), Blue (fish), Yellow (oilseeds), others**.
**Low & volatile incomes, indebtedness, fragmented holdings, farmer suicides, climate risk**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: agri strategy, policy & agrarian crisis

items: **Green Revolution (late 1960s, MS Swaminathan/Norman Borlaug)** — HYV wheat & rice → self-sufficiency, but regionally skewed (Punjab/Haryana), water/soil stress, inequity; later **White (milk — Operation Flood, Verghese Kurien), Yellow (oilseeds), Blue (fish), Rainbow** revolutions.
**Agrarian crisis**: small/fragmented holdings, low productivity, monsoon dependence, indebtedness & farmer suicides, price volatility, inadequate MSP realisation, post-harvest losses.
**Reforms**: **e-NAM, FPOs (10,000 FPO scheme), contract farming, doubling farmers' income (Dalwai Committee), PM-KISAN, PMFBY (crop insurance)**; the repealed 2020 farm laws episode.
**Sustainable agri**: natural/organic farming (**Andhra Pradesh Community Managed Natural Farming — ZBNF**, a national model), millets ('Shree Anna', 2023 Int'l Year of Millets).
Revolutions: Green (grain), White (milk-Kurien), Blue (fish), Yellow (oilseeds).
Agrarian crisis drivers; Swaminathan Commission MSP = C2 + 50%.

prelimsPointers: **White Revolution / Operation Flood** — milk (**Verghese Kurien**, Amul/NDDB).
**Blue (fish), Yellow (oilseeds), Golden (horticulture/honey), Silver (eggs/poultry)** revolutions.
**M.S. Swaminathan Commission (NCF)** — recommended **MSP = C2 cost + 50%**.
Agrarian distress — **indebtedness, fragmented holdings, price volatility, farmer suicides**.
**e-NAM** — electronic National Agriculture Market (unified mandi platform).
**FPOs (Farmer Producer Organisations)** aggregate small farmers.
Goal of **doubling farmers' income** (Dalwai Committee).

**AP Community-Managed Natural Farming (ZBNF)** = national model for sustainable agriculture.

blocks.text: **Land reforms** (abolition of intermediaries, tenancy reform, ceilings, consolidation), **institutional agricultural credit**, and **Minimum Support Price (MSP)** are the three pillars of India's effort to make farming equitable and remunerative.

rows: **Abolition of zamindari/intermediaries, tenancy reform, land ceilings, consolidation of holdings, cooperative farming**.
**Cooperatives, RRBs, commercial banks, NABARD (apex), Kisan Credit Card**; priority-sector lending.
Price floor announced by govt (on **CACP** advice) for ~**23 crops**; procurement by FCI.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: land reforms, credit & MSP

items: **Land reforms (post-1947)**: abolition of **zamindari/intermediaries**, **tenancy reforms** (security, fair rent), **land ceilings** & redistribution, **consolidation** of holdings, and **Bhoodan/Gramdan (Vinoba Bhave)** — success uneven (best in Kerala/WB).

**Agricultural credit**: institutional (**cooperatives — PACS, RRBs, commercial banks, NABARD (apex, 1982)**) vs non-institutional (moneylenders); **Kisan Credit Card (KCC)**, priority-sector lending, interest subvention; farm-loan waivers.

**MSP (Minimum Support Price)**: announced by **CACP** for **23 crops**; procurement mainly wheat & rice via **FCI**; A2+FL & C2 cost concepts (Swaminathan's C2+50% demand); **decentralised procurement, PDS/NFSA** linkage.
**Marketing**: APMC mandis, e-NAM, warehousing (WDRA), Essential Commodities Act.
Land reform components (intermediary abolition, tenancy, ceiling, consolidation).
MSP recommended by CACP for ~23 crops; NABARD = apex agri-credit; KCC.

blocks.text: Despite food-grain self-sufficiency, India faces **persistent malnutrition** (stunting, wasting, anaemia). **Food security** — ensured through the **National Food Security Act (2013), PDS and nutrition schemes** — remains a central welfare goal.

rows: Legal right to subsidised foodgrains to **~two-thirds of the population** (75% rural, 50% urban).
Public Distribution System; **One Nation One Ration Card** for portability.
**POSHAN Abhiyaan, ICDS/Anganwadi, Mid-Day Meal (PM POSHAN), fortification**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: food security & malnutrition

items: **Food security dimensions**: availability, access, absorption/utilisation, stability; **NFSA 2013** — legal right to subsidised grain for ~**67%** of population (75% rural, 50% urban), **PDS/TPDS**, One Nation One Ration Card.
**Buffer stock & procurement**: **FCI**, MSP, minimum buffer norms; issues — leakages, storage losses (now DBT/PDS reforms).

**Malnutrition**: India's triple burden — **undernutrition (stunting/wasting/underweight — NFHS-5), micronutrient deficiency ('hidden hunger'), and rising obesity**; anaemia widespread among women & children.
**Interventions**: **POSHAN Abhiyaan, ICDS/Anganwadi, PM POSHAN (Mid-Day Meal), fortification of rice/salt/oil, Eat Right India**; global — Global Hunger Index (India debates methodology).
NFSA 2013 = legal food-grain right to ~2/3 population; ONORC portability.
Malnutrition = stunting/wasting/anaemia; POSHAN Abhiyaan; NFHS data.

prelimsPointers: **National Food Security Act (2013)** covers **~67%** of the population (75% rural, 50% urban).

**Eat Right India, Poshan Vatika** are supporting initiatives.
